rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Indifference to prayer and zakāh shows that people lack conviction in the Hereafter; anyone claiming otherwise is lying.
rows.anchor: those who are indifferent to the prayer and zakāh are in fact deprived of the conviction in the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those described as guided by their Lord will succeed in the Hereafter; all others are astray and will be cast into Hell.
rows.anchor: All the rest are in error and shall be flung into Hell in the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word اِشْتِرَاء can mean giving preference.
rows.anchor: also means to give preference, as has been explained at relevant places in this exegesis.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression “idle talk” parallels Qurʾānic “varnished speech” (6:112) and is set against the wise Book’s revelations.
rows.anchor: is much similar in construction to زخرف القول used in the Qur’ān (6:112).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Idle talk” refers to the baseless notions the opponents spread to turn people away from God’s revelations.
rows.anchor: it would refer to all those things which the miscreants of those times would spread in order to lead people away from the revelations of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān directs people to face life’s facts, while its opponents keep them occupied with foolish distractions.
rows.anchor: The Qur’ān wanted people to face the real facts of life but its opponents wanted its addressees to remain entangled in the foolish things they were occupied with.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse expresses wonder that people prefer baseless concepts which support their desires and innovations over a wisdom-filled Book.
rows.anchor: they are giving preference to those baseless concepts which provide corroboration to their desires and innovations.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase about leading people astray without knowledge, “knowledge” means clear proof or argument.
rows.anchor: a clear proof or argument.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same word for knowledge occurs again in verse 30 and is explained there as well.
rows.anchor: This word also occurs in verse 30 ahead. It will be further explained there.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents’ efforts aim to block God’s path, though they have no sound proof for their own course; they still mock revelation and embellish baseless ideas.
rows.anchor: they have no sound proof of the path they are treading by leaving the path of God and which they also want people to tread.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The humiliating punishment contrasts with the believers’ guidance and success, and awaits those spreading baseless notions and innovations.
rows.anchor: The words say that a very humiliating punishment awaits them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their preference for arrogance over truth explains the humiliation: humiliation is the punishment of arrogance before God.
rows.anchor: This is because in opposition to the truth their bias is towards arrogance and the punishment of arrogance before God is humiliation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishments vary, but the worst is the kind that humiliates and disgraces its recipients.
rows.anchor: the worst punishment is the one which humiliates and disgraces people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrogant turn away when God’s revelations are recited, behaving as if they have not heard and their ears are deaf; they treat the revelations as insignificant.
rows.anchor: such is the situation of these people that when God’s revelations are recited to them, they turn their backs with great arrogance and walk away, as if they did not even hear them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they deem revelation unworthy of attention, the Prophet is told on God’s behalf to announce a painful doom for them.
rows.anchor: if their arrogance has increased so much that God’s revelations are not worthy enough to pay heed to, then the Prophet (sws), on God’s behalf, should sound them glad tidings of a painful doom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mere indifference can be corrected by reminders, but continued arrogance after admonition is incurable and leads to Hell.
rows.anchor: if this matter relates only to indifference, it can be reformed through reminding and admonishing them. However, if they show arrogance even after being reminded and admonished, then this ailment cannot be cured.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In contrast, believers who profess faith and do righteous deeds receive gardens of bliss in which they remain forever.
rows.anchor: These verses, in contrast, state the reward of people who profess faith in God’s revelations and befittingly follow them in their lives.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording says God’s promise of this reward is certain to be fulfilled.
rows.anchor: mean that this is a certain promise of God that is bound to be fulfilled.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise receives double emphasis because the preceding verse says the arrogant mock God’s revelations.
rows.anchor: make fun of God’s revelations. It is obvious that this ridicule was directed at

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ridicule targeted Qurʾānic promises that the poor and helpless Muslims of that time would inherit an eternal kingdom, so believers are assured the promise will stand.
rows.anchor: the helpless and poor among the Muslims of those times were given glad tidings of an eternal kingdom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s attributes of might and wisdom establish the certainty of His promise: failing to punish oppressors and reward the righteous would contradict those attributes.
rows.anchor: substantiate the certainty of God’s promise through His attributes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God did not punish oppressors and reward the righteous, He would be powerless and unwise, and the world would be purposeless; the author says this is self-evidently false.
rows.anchor: if God does not punish the arrogant and the oppressors and not reward the believers and the righteous, it would mean

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe’s signs show that its creator has absolute power and that His actions also display immense wisdom.
rows.anchor: observing which even a person of average intellect will be compelled to confess that the creator of this universe is

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse points to the heavens raised without visible pillars, mountains that keep the earth from reeling, diverse creatures, and rain that produces beneficial growth.
rows.anchor: God has spread living beings of various sorts and to nourish and nurture them has rained down water from the skies.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “without pillars that you can see,” the clause “you can see” qualifies “pillars”; the heavens are supported by pillars that remain invisible.
rows.anchor: In other words, this great roof has been raised high by its great creator with pillars

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has joined the parts of the universe through gravitational laws that only He can see.
rows.anchor: He has bound together the various portions of this universe with such laws of gravity which are seen only by Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The precise linguistic sense of “noble” here is “beneficial,” and the phrase points to God’s mercy and providence.
rows.anchor: is “beneficial.” This expression alludes to God’s mercy and providence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage openly challenges idolaters to produce those they associate with God; the same challenge recurs at 34:27 when their claim is baseless and the truth has been fully conveyed.
rows.anchor: This is an open challenge thrown to the Idolaters; they should bring forth in the open those whom they associate with God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged deities have no authority in the heavens or earth, as also stated at the opening of this sūrah.
rows.anchor: the Idolaters ascribe partners to God whereas they have not the slightest of authority in the heavens and the earth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deities had no share in creating the heavens and earth; 18:51 is cited to say God did not summon them to help create them.
rows.anchor: these deities have no share in the creation of the heavens and the earth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not seek their help to govern the universe; He alone runs its affairs without burden, refuting the idea that distant earth is administered by partners.
rows.anchor: He alone is solely running these affairs, and this does not burden him at all.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No intercession has weight before God unless He permits it; the intercessor may speak only for a person covered by that permission.
rows.anchor: no one’s intercession will have any weight before God except for whom He allows.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elsewhere the Qurʾān says an authorized intercessor will speak only the truth, never falsehood or anything contrary to truth.
rows.anchor: whatever such an intercessor will say will be the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rejects the idolaters’ belief that the angels they worship are God’s daughters and can persuade their father, who then listens out of love.
rows.anchor: the angels they worshipped that they are daughters of God and hence they can convince their father in favour of anything they want to

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word فُزِّعَ means to strike fear; with the preposition عَنْ it means to remove fear.
rows.anchor: is to strike fear; however, when it is used with the preposition

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels will be seized by dread on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: like all other creatures they too will be struck with dread and fear

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ dread leaves them unaware of God’s verdict about people, much less able to cajole Him for intercession.
rows.anchor: so that they will not even know what verdict has been passed by the Almighty regarding people – what to speak of cajoling the Almighty in favour of their intercession.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When their fear is removed, the angels ask what their Lord directed and are told that the directive is the truth.
rows.anchor: The reply will be whatever has been ordered is the truth in its entirety.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author connects this scene with 39:67–68, which describes the Day of Judgment and the trumpet blasts.
rows.anchor: While refuting this very notion of the Idolaters about the angels, the words used in Sūrah Zumar are:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the first blast all creatures in heaven and earth fall unconscious, except those God keeps secure.
rows.anchor: when the trumpet is sounded for the first time all creatures of heavens and the earth will fall down unconscious.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those God secures are associated with people who will not suffer the greatest horror (21:103).
rows.anchor: Such people are mentioned thus in the Qur’ān:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the second blast everyone rises and looks around in alarm; the author takes the angels’ question as occurring at this stage.
rows.anchor: It seems that it will be at this stage that the angels will ask the question stated in the verse as:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ question shows their terror: they are dumbstruck and ask others about God’s directive rather than initiating intercession.
rows.anchor: Thus they will themselves be dumbstruck at the situation, what to speak of taking the initiative in interceding for someone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited details concern the same occasion and context, though their true nature cannot be comprehended in this world.
rows.anchor: Their true nature cannot be comprehended in this world but both these verses are of the same occasion and context.
